mainTopic: Benefit from בגדי כהונה, the story of שמעון הצדיק and Alexander, and the כהן גדול's Torah reading on יום כפור
overview: The גמרא asks whether a כהן may get personal benefit from בגדי כהונה. It first tries to prove this from a משנה that says כהנים fold their garments and put them 'under their heads.' רב פפא rejects the proof by reading 'next to their heads,' and רב משרשיא learns from this that placing תפילין beside you while sleeping is fine. The גמרא supports רב פפא: lying on the garments would mean lying on the כלאים of the אבנט, which חכמים forbade even with ten mattresses in between. רב אשי disagrees and says the garments really were under their heads, because stiff כלאים is not forbidden. A ברייתא then proves directly that בגדי כהונה were given for benefit, though they may not be worn outside the מקדש. The גמרא challenges that limit with the story of שמעון הצדיק, who wore the vestments to meet Alexander and saved the מקדש from the כותים. It gives two answers: the clothes were only fit to be בגדי כהונה, or this was a time of עת לעשות לה׳. Finally the גמרא returns to the יום כפור Torah reading, discussing the passing of the ספר תורה and beginning a question about whether the כהן גדול was sitting, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The first clause was needed because of the latter clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on an earlier proof. It explains that the משנה's rule against sleeping in priestly garments was needed only because the next clause allows placing them under the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that first line was needed because of the latter part: 'They take off the garments, fold them, and place them under their heads.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on an attempt to prove something from the first part of a משנה. It says that first part was written only because of what the משנה says next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone tried to learn from the line 'they did not sleep in the holy garments' that using בגדי כהונה for benefit is forbidden. The גמרא answers that this line had a different job. The latter clause lets the garments go under the head, so you might have thought sleeping in them is also fine. The first line is there to block that mistake, so it proves nothing about the general benefit question.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
It was needed for it; it was written because of this

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new rule. It explains why an earlier line of the משנה exists, so that line cannot be used as a proof.

phrases.english: And it was needed because of the latter clause:
phrases.notes: The first part is there so we don't get the wrong idea from the later part.

phrases.english: They take off, fold, and place them under their heads.
phrases.notes: Quoting the latter clause of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an attempted proof from the first clause of the משנה, which came on the previous amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof drawn from the first clause ('they did not sleep in the holy garments').
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first clause was needed for a different reason: to stop people from drawing a wrong conclusion from the latter clause. So it says nothing about the general benefit question.

steps.title: Attempted proof from the latter clause that benefit is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now tries to prove from the latter clause itself that a person may benefit from בגדי כהונה, since the garments are used as a pillow.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They take them off, fold them, and place them under their heads.' Learn from this that בגדי כהונה were given to be benefited from!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the latter clause into a proof. If the כהנים may use the garments as a pillow, it seems benefit from them is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Resting your head on something is clear personal benefit. If the משנה allows it, then בגדי כהונה must not carry a ban on benefit. This seems to settle the question the גמרא has been asking.

keyTerms.meaning: They were given to be benefited from (benefit is allowed)

phrases.english: They take off, fold, and place
them under their heads,
learn from this
that priestly garments were given to be benefited from!

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ בִּגְדֵי כְּהוּנָּה נִיתְּנוּ לֵיהָנוֹת בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having moved the focus to the latter clause, the גמרא now tries to draw a proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: That benefit from בגדי כהונה is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's statement that כהנים place the folded garments under their heads.

steps.title: רב פפא rereads the משנה as 'next to their heads'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the proof. He says the משנה means the garments are placed beside the head, not under it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Do not say 'under their heads.' Rather, say 'next to their heads.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא knocks down the proof by changing how we read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the garments are only placed beside the head, the כהן is not lying on them and gets no real benefit. So the משנה no longer proves that benefit is allowed. The question is settled later by a ברייתא in Step 12.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not changing the law of the משנה on his own. He is showing that 'under their heads' should be understood as 'next to their heads.'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Do not say 'under their heads,'
rather say 'next to their heads.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא תַּחַת רָאשֵׁיהֶן, אֶלָּא אֵימָא כְּנֶגֶד רָאשֵׁיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the latter clause that benefit is permitted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the garments were used as a pillow. In fact they were only placed beside the head.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: placing תפילין at your side is fine
steps.stepSummary: Building on רב פפא's reading, רב משרשיא learns that a person may put his תפילין beside his head while sleeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: Learn from this that putting תפילין to the side is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא takes רב פפא's reading and draws a practical rule from it about תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets כהנים put their holy garments right beside their heads while sleeping. It does not worry that they will roll over onto them in their sleep. In the same way, a person may put his תפילין beside his head at night without worrying that he will roll onto them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine; it is proper

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a practical halachic source: תפילין may be kept beside one's head while sleeping.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
Learn from this
that putting phylacteries to the side is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side lesson drawn from רב פפא's reading in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Placing תפילין beside one's head while sleeping is permitted. We do not worry that one will roll onto them.

steps.title: Support for 'next to their heads' from the problem of כלאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב פפא. Lying on the garments would be forbidden because of כלאים in the אבנט, even if benefit were generally allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it is logical that it means 'next to their heads.' For if you thought 'under their heads,' I would forbid it anyway because of כלאים, since the belt is among them. And even if they were given to be benefited from, here he would be benefiting from כלאים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב פפא's reading with a logical argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אבנט (belt) is woven from wool and linen together, which is כלאים. Lying on כלאים is forbidden on its own, apart from any question about benefit from holy garments. So the משנה could not have allowed putting the garments under the head. It must mean beside the head.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (introduces support)
For if it entered your mind
A forbidden mixture of wool and linen (שעטנז)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate issues here. One is benefit from holy garments, which might be allowed. The other is כלאים, which is forbidden no matter what. The second problem stands even if the first is solved.

phrases.english: So too it is logical that it means next to their heads,
for if it entered your mind 'under their heads,'
I would derive it is forbidden because of diverse kinds,
since there is the belt.
And even granting that they were given to be benefited from,
he is still benefiting from diverse kinds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רב משרשיא's side point to support רב פפא's reading in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's reading: 'next to their heads.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: the אבנט contains כלאים, so lying on the garments would be forbidden whether or not benefit from them is allowed.

steps.title: The כלאים argument depends on a dispute about the אבנט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the כלאים argument depends on a מחלוקת about whether the ordinary כהן's אבנט was the same as the כהן גדול's. Under one view, the 'under their heads' reading seems to have no answer. רב אשי offers one later, in Step 10.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says the כהן גדול's belt is the same as the ordinary כהן's belt. But for the one who says the כהן גדול's belt is not the same as the ordinary כהן's belt, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the כלאים argument against two opinions about the ordinary כהן's belt. It shows the 'under their heads' reading has an answer under one view but not under the other. This sets up the next move of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת about whether the ordinary כהן's belt matches the belt the כהן גדול wears on יום כפור, which is plain linen. Under the view that they match, the ordinary belt has no כלאים, so lying on the garments could be fine. Under the other view the ordinary belt is כלאים, and then the 'under their heads' reading has no answer.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says
What is there to say? (no answer yet)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is read as 'next to their heads' (רב פפא). This is supported by the problem of lying on the כלאים of the אבנט, and that support depends on the dispute about what the ordinary כהן's belt was made of.

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who said
the belt of the High Priest

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הוּא אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: is the same as the belt of an ordinary priest.
But according to the one who said
the belt of the High Priest

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זֶה הוּא אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: is not the same as the belt of an ordinary priest,
what is there to say?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל זֶה הוּא אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the כלאים argument from step 5 against the dispute about the אבנט.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'under their heads' (that כהנים may lie on their garments).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the view that the ordinary כהן's belt contains כלאים, lying on the garments would mean lying on כלאים. So the 'under their heads' reading has no defense under that view.

steps.title: Spreading כלאים beneath you is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible escape: maybe כלאים is only forbidden to wear, not to lie on. A ברייתא shows that חכמים forbade even lying on כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: כלאים is only forbidden when you wear it or put it on top of you, but spreading it under you is permitted. But a ברייתא taught: 'It shall not come upon you' means that you may spread it beneath you. But the חכמים said it is forbidden to do so, in case a single thread wraps itself onto his body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is strengthening the proof for רב פפא. It answers someone who might say that lying on כלאים is allowed anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lying on כלאים were allowed, the כהנים could sleep on their garments and the כלאים argument would fall apart. The ברייתא admits that the Torah only forbids כלאים 'upon you'. But חכמים forbade spreading it under you, because a thread might wrap around the body, and that would count as wearing it.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing a garment on top of oneself, like a cover
Spreading something beneath oneself to lie on
'It shall not come upon you', the פסוק forbidding כלאים
A thread may wrap around (the body)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. מדאורייתא, spreading כלאים under you is permitted. Only מדרבנן is it forbidden.

phrases.english: And if you will say: כלאים, in wearing and placing on top,
is what is forbidden, but spreading it beneath is permitted,
but was it not taught: 'It shall not come upon you',
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא יט:יט.

phrases.english: but you are permitted to spread it beneath you.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: אָסוּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן,
phrases.english: But the Sages said: it is forbidden to do so,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא תִּיכָּרֵךְ נִימָא אַחַת עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ.
phrases.english: lest a single thread wrap itself onto his flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to Step 5's כלאים argument and protects it from a possible counterclaim.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that lying on כלאים is permitted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the rabbinic decree against spreading כלאים beneath oneself.

steps.title: A barrier in between does not help
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the כהן could put something between himself and the garments. No: even ten mattresses on top of כלאים do not permit sleeping on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that he puts something in between, did not רבי שמעון בן פזי say in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of רבי, in the name of the holy community in Jerusalem: Even if there are ten mattresses one on top of the other with כלאים underneath them, it is forbidden to sleep on them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a second escape route. The כהן cannot solve the problem by putting a barrier between himself and the כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a barrier, no thread could ever touch the body, so you might think the decree does not apply. But the קהלא קדישא ruled that even ten mattresses do not help. The decree applies across the board, even where the original worry is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy community in Jerusalem, a group of חכמים

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפְסֵיק לֵיהּ מִידֵּי בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי —
phrases.english: And if you will say that he places something in between,
but did not Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi say
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מִשּׁוּם קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: that Rabbi said in the name of the holy community in Jerusalem:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עֶשֶׂר מַצָּעוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ
phrases.english: Even ten mattresses, one on top of the other,
with כלאים beneath them,
it is forbidden to sleep upon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפְסֵיק לֵיהּ מִידֵּי בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the last loophole left after Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that a barrier permits lying on כלאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The decree applies even when many layers separate the person from the כלאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון בן פזי quoting the קהלא קדישא

steps.title: So the garments were beside their heads
steps.stepSummary: Since lying on the garments is forbidden, the משנה must mean beside their heads, just as רב פפא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that it means beside their heads? Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes this line of reasoning. The משנה means the garments were placed beside the כהנים' heads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every way of putting the garments under the head was blocked by כלאים. So רב פפא's reading wins, and the משנה gives no proof that benefit from בגדי כהונה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that...? (leads into a conclusion)
Learn from it; the point is proven

phrases.english: Rather, must one not learn from this:
beside their heads. Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from Steps 7 and 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה means beside their heads, as רב פפא said.

steps.title: רב אשי: really under their heads, because the garments are stiff
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the משנה as really meaning under their heads. There is no כלאים problem, because בגדי כהונה are stiff.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Actually, it means under their heads. And if you ask that they are benefiting from כלאים, the answer is that בגדי כהונה are stiff.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with the conclusion of Step 9. He says the garments really could have been under the כהנים' heads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on כלאים applies to soft cloth that wraps around the body and gives warmth. Stiff material does not wrap around you, so it is not forbidden. This removes the whole כלאים objection, and 'under their heads' is possible again.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם תַּחַת רָאשֵׁיהֶן,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Actually, under their heads,
and as for the objection that he benefits from כלאים,
priestly garments are stiff.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם תַּחַת רָאשֵׁיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 9's conclusion by removing the כלאים problem.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה must mean 'beside their heads'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed that the כלאים ban applies to stiff garments.

steps.title: Support: stiff felt from נרש is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's idea matches רב הונא's ruling that the stiff felt made in נרש is permitted even though it contains כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב הונא the son of רבי יהושע said: This stiff felt from נרש is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אשי's idea with an earlier ruling about stiff felt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא permitted a stiff כלאים felt because it does not wrap around the body. That is exactly the principle רב אשי uses for בגדי כהונה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Like that which Rav Huna, son of Rabbi Yehoshua, said:
This stiff felt of Neresh is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's claim from Step 10.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא בריה דרבי יהושע on the felt of נרש

steps.title: A ברייתא: בגדי כהונה were given for benefit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that the כהנים may wear their garments in the מקדש even when they are not serving, because בגדי כהונה were given to be benefited from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: As for בגדי כהונה, one who goes out wearing them into the country is forbidden. But in the מקדש, whether during the service or not during the service, it is permitted, because בגדי כהונה were given to be benefited from.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turned out to be unclear. So the גמרא brings a new source that answers the original question directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing the garments in the מקדש when not serving is pure personal benefit, and the ברייתא allows it. It even gives the reason openly: the garments were given for benefit. Only leaving the מקדש in them is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; brings a new source as proof
The country, meaning anywhere outside the מקדש
Were given to be benefited from

steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question the sugya opened with. The answer does not depend on the unclear reading of the משנה.

phrases.english: Come and hear: priestly garments,
one who goes out in them to the country is forbidden.
But in the Temple, whether during the service
or not during the service, it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה נִיתְּנוּ לֵיהָנוֹת בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: because priestly garments were given to be benefited from.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה, הַיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן לַמְּדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debate over the משנה and proves the original question from a different source.
steps.raayaObject: It is permitted to benefit from בגדי כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about wearing בגדי כהונה in the מקדש

steps.title: Proven: benefit from בגדי כהונה is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the ברייתא's proof. It is permitted to benefit from בגדי כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states the reason openly, so it cannot be pushed aside. Benefiting from בגדי כהונה is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about sleeping with the garments is unclear: 'beside their heads' (רב פפא) or 'under their heads' (רב אשי, since stiff כלאים is allowed). But the ברייתא clearly proves that בגדי כהונה were given for benefit.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof brought in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is permitted to benefit from בגדי כהונה.

steps.title: Is it really forbidden to wear the vestments outside the Temple?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the rule that בגדי כהונה may not be worn במדינה. It cites a ברייתא about יום הר גרזים, a day on which eulogies are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And outside the Temple, is it not allowed? But it was taught in a ברייתא: the 25th of טבת is the Day of Mount גרזים, on which eulogizing is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that בגדי כהונה may not be worn outside the מקדש. It begins quoting a ברייתא, and the challenge itself will come from the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא only allowed the vestments inside the מקדש, which implies they are forbidden במדינה. The גמרא now brings a source about a joyful day, יום הר גרזים. The full story behind that day will show a כהן גדול wearing the vestments outside. This line only opens the source; the evidence comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the 'country', meaning anywhere outside the מקדש
'but wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?' This introduces a source used to challenge
the Day of Mount גרזים, the 25th of טבת, a celebration day
to eulogize. Eulogies are not given on joyful days

steps.confusionAlert: The fact that eulogies are banned is not the challenge itself. It only identifies the day. The real challenge comes from the story in the next step, where שמעון הצדיק wears בגדי כהונה outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: And in the country (outside the Temple), not?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking about what the ברייתא in Step 12 seems to imply.

phrases.english: But was it not taught:
phrases.notes: This source comes from מגילת תענית.

phrases.english: On the twenty-fifth [of Tevet]
[is] the Day of Mount Gerizim,
on which one may not eulogize?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implied limit in the ברייתא of Step 12, which allowed the vestments only inside the מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that בגדי כהונה may not be worn במדינה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records an event in which the vestments were worn outside the מקדש, which suggests this is permitted.

steps.title: שמעון הצדיק goes out wearing the priestly vestments
steps.stepSummary: The כותים get permission to destroy the בית המקדש. שמעון הצדיק puts on בגדי כהונה and goes out at night with the leaders of ישראל to meet אלכסנדרוס מוקדון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was the day the כותים asked אלכסנדרוס מוקדון for our G-d's House so they could destroy it, and he gave it to them. People came and told שמעון הצדיק. What did he do? He put on the priestly garments and wrapped himself in them. The noblemen of ישראל went with him, carrying torches. All night long, these people walked from one side and those people walked from the other side, until dawn rose.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells the story behind יום הר גרזים. Its key detail is that שמעון הצדיק wore בגדי כהונה outside the מקדש. This is the actual evidence behind the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון הצדיק traveled far from the מקדש to meet the king, and he deliberately wore the בגדי כהונה. If the vestments were forbidden outside the מקדש, how could the כהן גדול do this? That detail is what makes the story a problem for the earlier ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the Samaritans, enemies of the Jews at that time
the כהן גדול of that period
the noblemen or leaders of ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: The two words לָבַשׁ בִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה are the heart of the challenge. They show a כהן גדול wearing the vestments במדינה.

phrases.english: The day that the Samaritans requested
the House of our God
from Alexander the Macedonian, in order to destroy it,
and they gave it to them.
phrases.notes: In other words, they were granted permission to destroy it.

phrases.english: People came and informed Shimon HaTzaddik.
What did he do?
He put on the priestly garments,
phrases.notes: This is the key detail for the challenge.

phrases.english: and wrapped himself in the priestly garments,
and some of the nobles of Israel were with him,
with torches of fire in their hands.
And all night long,
these were walking from this side,
phrases.notes: This refers to the Jewish group.

phrases.english: and those were walking from that side,
phrases.notes: This refers to Alexander's army and the כותים.

phrases.english: until dawn broke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא opened in Step 14 and supplies the actual evidence for the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That בגדי כהונה may be worn outside the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of מגילת תענית, which says שמעון הצדיק wore the vestments when he went out to meet אלכסנדרוס.

steps.title: Alexander bows before שמעון הצדיק
steps.stepSummary: At dawn the כותים tell Alexander that the approaching group are rebels. When the two camps meet at אנטיפטרס, Alexander bows to שמעון הצדיק. He explains that this man's image leads him to victory in battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: When dawn rose, Alexander asked the כותים, 'Who are these people?' They said, 'Jews who rebelled against you.' When he reached אנטיפטרס, the sun shone and the two groups met. When he saw שמעון הצדיק, he got down from his chariot and bowed before him. His people said, 'Should a great king like you bow to this Jew?!' He answered, 'The image of this man's face goes before me and wins my battles.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story. It describes the meeting between Alexander and שמעון הצדיק and the king's surprising respect for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כותים try to turn the king against the Jews by calling them rebels. Instead, Alexander recognizes שמעון הצדיק as the figure he sees in his victories, and he honors him. This adds no new halachic point. It is the continuation of the source being quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: Antipatris, a town where the two groups met

phrases.english: Once dawn broke,
he (Alexander) said to them: Who are these?
They (the Samaritans) said to him: Jews who rebelled against you.
When he reached Antipatris,
the sun shone and they met each other.
When he saw Shimon HaTzaddik,
he got down from his chariot and bowed before him.
They (his escorts) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל כְּמוֹתְךָ יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לִיהוּדִי זֶה?!
phrases.english: Should a great king like you bow to this Jew?!
He said to them:
The image of this man's face
leads me to victory on my battlefield.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the narrative of the ברייתא from the point of dawn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: Alexander honors שמעון הצדיק and refuses to treat him as a rebel.

steps.title: The Jews plead for the Temple and the כותים are handed over
steps.stepSummary: The Jews explain that the כותים misled the king into destroying the house where Jews pray for him and his kingdom. Alexander hands the כותים over to the Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked them, 'Why have you come?' They said, 'Is it possible that the House where we pray for you and your kingdom, that it not be destroyed, should be the target of gentiles who mislead you into destroying it?' He asked, 'Who are they?' They answered, 'These כותים standing before you.' He said, 'They are handed over into your hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its turning point. The Jews explain the danger, and Alexander gives the כותים into their power. This explains why the day became a celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jews argue that destroying the בית המקדש would also harm the king, since prayers for his kingdom are offered there. Alexander is convinced and reverses his decision against the כותים. This rescue is the reason the 25th of טבת was made a day without eulogies.

keyTerms.meaning: handed over into your hands, yours to deal with

steps.whatToRemember: This ברייתא is being used as a קשיא. שמעון הצדיק wore בגדי כהונה outside the מקדש, which seems to contradict the earlier ruling that they may be worn only inside the מקדש. The גמרא answers this challenge in Steps 19-20, after the story ends.

phrases.english: He said to them (the Jews): Why have you come?
They said: Is it possible that a House
in which we pray for you
and for your kingdom, that it not be destroyed,
gentiles will mislead you into destroying it?
He said to them: Who are these (who misled me)?
They said to him: These Samaritans,
who are standing before you.
He said to them:
Behold, they are handed over into your hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the dialogue between Alexander and the Jews after he bows to שמעון הצדיק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: Alexander hands the כותים over to the Jews, saving the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The punishment of the כותים and the new יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The Jews punish the כותים by dragging them to הר גרזים. They plow over the mountain and sow it with a lowly crop, and that day becomes a יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away they pierced the כותים in their heels and tied them to their horses' tails. They kept dragging them over thorns and thistles until they reached הר גרזים. When they reached הר גרזים, they plowed it over and sowed it with כרשינין. This was exactly what the כותים had wanted to do to the House of our God. They made that day a יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the story it began in step 14. It explains why יום הר גרזים became a holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment matches the crime: the כותים wanted to plow over the בית המקדש, so their own temple on הר גרזים was plowed over instead. The point for our סוגיא is the whole story taken together. שמעון הצדיק wore בגדי כהונה far outside the מקדש. That seems to contradict the rule that בגדי כהונה may not be worn במדינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Gerizim, the site of the כותים's temple
Vetch, a lowly plant used as animal feed (Sefaria translates it as leeks); planting it shows total destruction
A festival or day of celebration

phrases.english: Immediately they pierced them in their heels
and hung them on their horses' tails,
and they kept dragging them
over the thorns and over the thistles,
until they reached Mount Gerizim.
Once they reached Mount Gerizim —
they plowed it and sowed it with vetch,
phrases.notes: Some take כרשינין to mean 'leeks'. Either way, it shows total destruction.

phrases.english: just as they had sought to do to the House of our God.
And that day they made into a festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from the ברייתא. Alexander has just handed the כותים over to the Jews.
steps.raayaObject: That בגדי כהונה may be worn outside the מקדש (against the ruling of the ברייתא in Step 12)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of יום הר גרזים, where שמעון הצדיק wore בגדי כהונה far outside the מקדש

steps.title: First answer: the clothes were only fit to be בגדי כהונה
steps.stepSummary: שמעון הצדיק did not wear real, holy בגדי כהונה. He wore clothes that were made like them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: they were clothes fit to be בגדי כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from the story. It says שמעון הצדיק's clothes only looked like בגדי כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against wearing בגדי כהונה outside applies only to real, sanctified garments. His clothes were the same material and design, but they were not sanctified. So no rule was broken.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say — introduces one possible answer
Fit or suitable (but not actually sanctified)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
they were fit to be priestly garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction that the story (Steps 14–18) created against the rule of the ברייתא in Step 12, which forbids wearing the vestments במדינה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the clothes were not real בגדי כהונה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמעון הצדיק wore real בגדי כהונה outside the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: He wore similar clothes that were not sanctified, so the rule is not contradicted.

steps.title: Second answer: an emergency allows breaking the rule
steps.stepSummary: He did wear real בגדי כהונה. Saving the מקדש was an emergency, and the פסוק of עת לעשות לה׳ allows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: "It is a time to act for ה׳; they have voided Your Torah."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer. Even if the clothes were real, an emergency to save the מקדש allowed him to wear them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer accepts that a real rule was set aside. The פסוק teaches that in a crisis, a law may be broken to protect the Torah itself. Saving the בית המקדש from destruction was such a crisis.

keyTerms.meaning: A time to act for ה׳ (תהלים קי״ט:קכ״ו)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the rule against wearing בגדי כהונה outside is cancelled. It is set aside only in a true emergency like this one.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
"It is a time to act for the Lord;
they have voided Your Torah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer instead of the first one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Emergency exception based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wearing real בגדי כהונה outside is always forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a crisis that threatens the Torah or the מקדש, the rule may be set aside.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for שמעון הצדיק: (1) the clothes were only fit to be בגדי כהונה, or (2) real ones were allowed because of עת לעשות לה׳.

steps.title: An inference from the passing of the ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The ספר תורה passes through lesser officials before reaching the כהן גדול. The גמרא suggests this proves one may honor a student in front of his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the synagogue attendant takes a ספר תורה and passes it up to the כהן גדול. Learn from this: we may give honor to a student in the presence of the teacher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the כהן גדול reading from the Torah. It tries to learn a general rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ספר תורה is handed to the חזן הכנסת, then to the ראש הכנסת, then to the סגן, all in front of the כהן גדול. The כהן גדול is like everyone's teacher. So it seems that honoring lesser people in front of the greater one is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this — introduces an inference
In the presence of the teacher

phrases.english: The synagogue attendant takes a Torah scroll:
Learn from this
that honor may be given to a student in the presence of the teacher!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ חוֹלְקִין כָּבוֹד לְתַלְמִיד בִּמְקוֹם הָרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא returns to analyzing the words of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That one may honor a student in front of his teacher
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's order of passing the ספר תורה up to the כהן גדול

steps.title: אביי: the whole process honors the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Passing the scroll up step by step is itself a way of honoring the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: All of it is for the honor of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back the proof from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officials are not really being honored on their own account. Passing the scroll through higher and higher ranks shows that the כהן גדול is the greatest of all. So we cannot learn anything about honoring a student in front of his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it — the whole process

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל הִיא.
phrases.english: The whole thing is for the honor of the High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי כּוּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 21.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The handing over is not honor for the officials. It is a ceremony that honors the כהן גדול himself.

steps.title: Was the כהן גדול sitting in the עזרה?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the כהן גדול stands to receive the scroll, which implies he was sitting until then. The גמרא begins to challenge this with another משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and the כהן גדול stands. This implies that until now he was sitting. But we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new challenge. The source it challenges from is quoted at the start of the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'he stands' suggest that the כהן גדול was sitting before. The גמרא is about to quote another משנה that seems to rule out sitting in that place. This step only sets up the question.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication — inferred from what was said
But didn't we learn in a משנה — introduces a contradicting source

phrases.english: And the High Priest stands.
This implies that he was sitting,
but didn't we learn in a mishna:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹמֵד מִכְּלָל שֶׁהוּא יוֹשֵׁב וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section analyzing the next words of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implication that the כהן גדול was sitting before he stood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה (quoted on the next amud) seems to forbid sitting there, so how could the כהן גדול have been sitting?
